meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
What, did you fall in love with her?
He fell in love at first sight.
That means you will fall in love soon.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

встать.gloss: to stand up, to get up

meanings.en: to stand up, to get up (out of bed)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stand up, to get up', paired with 'вставать'.

examples.text: Кто первый встал, того и тапки.
examples.trans: First come, first served (whoever got up first gets the slippers).

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: a brave person; also the main character of a story

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: an idiom for a big telling-off

meanings.en: 'голову оторвать' = to tear someone's head off
meanings.note: an idiom for a big telling-off

examples.trans: Mum will tear my head off.

examples.text: Какая тебе опергруппа? Мне твоя мать голову оторвёт.
examples.trans: What field team? Your mother will tear my head off.
The governor has come to the town.
And does the governor support you?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'blood pressure' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Those make your blood pressure rise.

examples.text: Давление? Ничего, от тебя у меня просто кружится голова.
examples.trans: Blood pressure? It's nothing, you just make my head spin.

examples.text: Девушки, как я, у тебя не будет!
examples.trans: You'll never have a girl like me!

meanings.note: belonging to children or from childhood

examples.trans: This is an old children's book.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'украсть'.

examples.trans: I'm not going to steal a dog.

examples.text: Я не могу спать спокойно! Этот старик крадёт у девушки лучшие годы.
examples.trans: I cannot sleep in peace! This old man is stealing the girl's best years.

meanings.note: голова кружится = one's head is spinning, one feels dizzy

examples.trans: The leaves are whirling in the wind.

examples.text: Алло, Люся, привет! У Лёвы голова кружится?
examples.trans: Hello, Lyusya, hi! Is Lyova's head spinning?

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

examples.text: Молодой человек, как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

examples.text: Молодой человек, а как на тест-драйв записаться?
examples.trans: Young man, how do I sign up for a test drive?

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?
He taught me how to swim.

examples.text: Ура, работает приёмчик! Это меня губернатор научил.
examples.trans: Hooray, the little trick works! The governor taught me this.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Russian uses one word for both
Russian uses one word for both

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over

examples.trans: He will hand over the money.

examples.text: Потом надо отдать москвичам твои деньги из подвала.
examples.trans: Then I have to give your money from the basement to the Moscow people.

meanings.note: перестань(те)! = stop it!, oh come on!

examples.text: Да перестаньте! Я двадцать лет в карты не играла.
examples.trans: Oh, stop it! I haven't played cards for twenty years.

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: the person helped is in the dative: 'помогать маме' = to help mum

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: head of a country or a company

examples.trans: The president is speaking on TV.
Who is the president of the company?

examples.text: Там же президент выступает! Надо открыть шампанское.
examples.trans: But the president is on TV! We have to open the champagne.
Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.

examples.trans: You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

examples.text: Ура, работает приёмчик! Это меня губернатор научил.
examples.trans: Hooray, the little trick works! The governor taught me this.

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Какая разница? = What difference does it make?

examples.text: Ну и что? Какая разница? Вика — моя жена.
examples.trans: So what? What difference does it make? Vika is my wife.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Сейчас через сад и мост — и дома.
examples.trans: Right now through the park and the bridge, and I'm home.
The children are walking in the town park.

examples.text: Да вот иду уже! Сейчас через сад и мост — и дома.
examples.trans: I'm walking already! Right now through the park and the bridge, and I'm home.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

снять.gloss: to film, to photograph; to take off; to rent

meanings.en: to film, to take a photo/video of

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон.
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone.
He took off his coat by the door.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон. И сразу все мне помогают!
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone. And right away everyone helps me!

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sleep', paired with 'поспать'.

examples.text: Ладно, утром позвоню ей. Поехали спать.
examples.trans: All right, I'll call her in the morning. Let's go to sleep.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.
This old man is sitting on the bench.
The old man told an interesting story.

examples.text: Я не могу спать спокойно! Этот старик крадёт у девушки лучшие годы.
examples.trans: I cannot sleep in peace! This old man is stealing the girl's best years.

meanings.note: Core Russian interj meaning 'stop' in everyday speech.
Common feminine noun meaning 'pill, tablet' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Марина, иди ко мне! Я сегодня принял одну таблетку.
examples.trans: Marina, come to me! I took a pill today.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: на улице = out on the street / outside
на улице холодно = it's cold outside

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.
There are reporters out on the street!

meanings.note: Core Russian interj meaning 'hooray, hurrah' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ура, работает приёмчик! Это меня губернатор научил.
examples.trans: Hooray, the little trick works! The governor taught me this.

фу.gloss: drop it! (to a dog); ugh, yuck

examples.text: Лютик, Лютик! Фу! Что ты там делаешь? Лютик, стой!
examples.trans: Lyutik, Lyutik! Drop it! What are you doing there? Lyutik, stop!

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: целую! = kisses! (at the end of a call or message)

examples.trans: Well, call me, kitten. Bye, kisses!

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Common substantive noun meaning 'noise' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты можешь убрать весь этот шум?
examples.trans: Can you cut out all this noise?
Where is this noise coming from?

examples.text: Так, ты можешь убрать весь этот шум? Нам нужен только Аникеев.
examples.trans: Right, can you cut out all this noise? We only need Anikeev.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
